descriptive_title: Grade 2 Mathematics: Demonstrations — Likelihood with Spinners and Dice (D2.1-D2.2)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.D2.1: use mathematical language, including the terms “impossible”, “possible”, and “certain”, to describe the likelihood of complementary events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions
curriculum_expectations.D2.2: make and test predictions about the likelihood that the mode(s) of a data set from one population will be the same for data collected from a different population

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 2 unit on likelihood and complementary events (D2.1, D2.2) framed around 'What Could Happen?' — Lucky Lou the Loon and Maybe Mae the Cat. Day 1 reviews impossible/possible/certain. Day 2 introduces COMPLEMENTARY events (one happens means the other doesn't). Day 3 explores spinners. Day 4 explores dice. Day 5 closes with a Mode Prediction Capstone. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will use likelihood vocabulary including complementary events, predict outcomes, and test mode predictions across populations.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Events are IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, or CERTAIN. We predict using likelihood.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Lucky reviews impossible/possible/certain; children predict events.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Complementary events: when ONE happens the OTHER doesn't. Heads OR tails. Rain OR no rain.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maybe Mae shows pairs; children name complements.

lesson_arc.big_idea: A SPINNER with bigger sections is MORE LIKELY to land there.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can predict spinner outcomes using likelihood.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Lucky spins and predicts; children make and test spinner predictions.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Dice rolls are POSSIBLE 1-6. We predict the MODE after many rolls.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can predict the mode of dice rolls.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Mae rolls and tracks the mode; children predict and test.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Detectives predict the MODE for one group, then test in ANOTHER group. Same mode? Different?
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can predict mode and test it across groups.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children survey 2 classes and compare modes.

recurring_characters.name: Lucky Lou the Loon
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Same Lucky from Grade 1; now tackles complementary events. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young Canadian loon with a tiny detective hat and magnifying glass. Holds a coin or die. Confident expression.

recurring_characters.name: Maybe Mae the Cat
recurring_characters.role: Lucky's partner. The 'maybe' character. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small striped cat with a question-mark patch on her vest. Holds a clipboard for predictions.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 2 likelihood adds COMPLEMENTARY events to G1 vocabulary.
Spinners introduce ALL POSSIBLE outcomes with section size = likelihood.
Mode prediction across populations is the main D2.2 idea.
Connect to scientific thinking — predict, test, observe.
canadian_context_notes: Canadian weather: rain or no rain (complementary).
Hockey: home win or away win (complementary).
Maple syrup season for spinner illustration.
